Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment uses GFP-trap affinity purification (AP-MS) to identify members of the PRPS complex. Acquisition is DDA based on the use of Sequest HT and Orbitrap Eclipse for peptide fragmentation spectra. Quantification is explicitly listed as peptide counting in PRIDE metadata. No specific PTM enrichment (like phospho or ubiquitylome) was performed; the identified PTMs in metadata (monohydroxylated, deamidated) are common artifacts/variable mods.

scope: The cell lysates were then clarified by centrifugation (15,000 × g, 15 mins, 4 °C) and incubated with the equilibrated anti-GFP nanobody conjugated to magnetic particles (Chromotek GFP-Trap® Magnetic Particles M-270) for 1 h on a rotator disk at 4 °C.

The beads were then boiled for 10 mins at 95°C in 2X SDS-sample buffer for protein elution. The eluates were sent to University of Cincinnati Proteomics Laboratory (UCPL) for mass spectrometry (MS) analysis.
Immunoprecipitation followed by LC-MS/MS peptide identification from all revealed that all PRPS homologs assemble into a single enzyme complex in human (HEK293T) cells.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The mass spectrometry analysis was performed on eluates from GFP immunoprecipitation (affinity purification) of the PRPS complex. While the text mentions the complex is cytosolic, 'cytosolic fraction' is not used to describe the material analyzed by MS, but rather the localization of the target.
